interpretation: The supported pooled pre-loss local-history signal does not persist among meter marks that become completely seagrass-bare in the loss year. This weakens a simple hidden below-ground legacy interpretation and suggests that the broader recovery association depends on community/habitat continuity or other state differences.
next_hypothesis: Test whether pre-loss focal-history information is conditional on loss-year vegetation continuity, using a frozen interaction between within-node centered run length and loss-year vegetated state.
claim_boundary: Post-hoc subgroup analysis of an already-opened recovery endpoint.
Do not claim residual rhizomes or clonal memory from the pooled history result after the bare-loss subgroup null.
The bare subgroup is modest (44 sequences, 8 returns); the null is informative but does not prove absence of below-ground persistence.
Return is recorded reappearance, not genet-level recolonization.
Do not relax subgroup minima or pool vegetated states back into this endpoint to rescue the legacy effect.
